description: The plot titled “Performance w.r.t. Temperature” shows Pass@8 accuracy as a function of generation temperature for three methods. The x-axis is labeled “Temperature,” uses a linear scale, and spans 0.1 to 1.0 with ticks at 0.1 intervals. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy (Pass@8),” uses a linear scale, and ranges from about 62.5 to 82.5 with tick marks every 2.5. The On-policy RL series is drawn in yellow with upward-pointing triangle markers connected by a solid line; it starts near 63.5 at temperature 0.1, rises to about 70.0 at 0.2, stays around 69–72 through 0.6, dips to about 67.5 at 0.7, peaks near 75.0 at 0.8, then ends around 73.5 at 1.0. The LUFFY series is red with star markers and a solid line; it begins around 76.0 at 0.1, increases to about 78.8 at 0.2, stays near 76–77 from 0.3 to 0.6, rises to about 79.8 at 0.7 and about 80.6 at 0.8, dips to about 78.8 at 0.9, and finishes near 80.6 at 1.0. The SFT series is teal with downward-pointing triangle markers and a solid line; it starts around 76.2 at 0.1, declines to about 75.2 at 0.2 and about 74.4 at 0.3–0.4, drops to about 70.0 at 0.5, rises back to about 76.0 at 0.6, falls to about 71.8 at 0.7, increases to about 73.6 at 0.8, dips to about 71.6 at 0.9, and ends around 74.4 at 1.0.
caption_used: The line plot illustrates Pass@8 accuracy across varying generation temperatures, measured on the merged sets of AIME 2024 and AMC. The 'On-policy RL' line (yellow, triangle markers) shows a steady increase from approximately 63.0 at 0.1 to 75.0 at 0.8, followed by a slight decline to 73.0 at 1.0. The 'LUFFY' line (red, star markers) demonstrates consistent superiority, starting at 76.0 at 0.1 and peaking at 81.0 at 0.8, before stabilizing at 80.0 at 1.0. The 'SFT' line (teal, inverted triangle markers) begins at 73.0 at 0.1, dips sharply to 68.0 at 0.5, and recovers to 74.0 at 1.0, showing the most variability among the three methods. Overall, LUFFY consistently outperforms the other methods across all temperature settings, with On-policy RL showing the most significant improvement over time.
